name: Kimi K3.1 Pro

lineage.how_derived: post-trained from Kimi K3 with large-scale joint reinforcement learning across hundreds of downstream domains; the first model of the K3.1 series (card)

purpose: The card calls it Moonshot's most capable 3T-class, natively multimodal open-weight agentic model, improved over K3 in coding, 3D creation, financial research and factual accuracy, with a 1M-token context.

license.name: Kimi K3.1-Pro License (modified MIT)
license.notes: LICENSE text read (3.1 KB). MIT-style grant including weights. Conditions: (2) a Model-as-a-Service business whose and affiliates' revenue exceeds US$20 million over 12 months needs a separate agreement with Moonshot before commercial use; (3) commercial products with more than 100 million monthly active users or more than US$20 million monthly revenue must display 'Kimi K3.1-Pro' in the UI; (4) internal use that does not expose the model to third parties is exempt. No territory exclusion. Contact license@moonshot.ai.

architecture.kind: sparse MoE with Kimi Delta Attention and gated DSA, latent MoE, MoonViT-V2 vision encoder
architecture.attention: 69 KDA linear-attention layers and 24 gated DSA (sparse indexed) layers, 96 heads, hidden 7168, DSA index top-k 2048
architecture.drafter: none shipped (num_nextn_predict_layers 0); a community drafter RadixArk/Kimi-K3.1-Dflash2-Preview exists
architecture.why_this_design: The card lists the configuration (2 shared experts, latent MoE dimension 3584, SiTU-GLU activation, MXFP4 weights with MXFP8 activations from quantisation-aware training) but gives no reasons for the layer split.

variants.notes: KLX-IQ1_M 647.87, KLX-IQ2_XXS 709.88 GB; file sizes only

variants.format: speculative drafter (finetune of the base per HF tags)

variants.notes: also nvidia NVFP4 and MLX repos; sizes not measured

pc-12gb.notes: smallest GGUF 592.7 GB against about 60 GB

pc-32gb.notes: 592.7 GB (IQ1_S) against about 158 GB (29.6 VRAM + 128 RAM); even 1 bit per weight of 2.8T parameters is about 350 GB

engine_support.notes: Community GGUFs exist; llama.cpp support was not verified. The card recommends vLLM, SGLang and TokenSpeed.

benchmarks.name: Terminal-Bench 4.0
benchmarks.variant: max effort, Claude Code harness (Opus 5.5 66.4, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 42.3)

strengths: Vendor lead among the open models on terminal and long-horizon coding tasks
Native MXFP4 QAT weights, so the 1.56 TB file is the intended precision
weaknesses: 2.8T parameters: nothing below a multi-GPU server can hold it
On DeepSWE and Program Bench the vendor's own table shows the 552B DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 at or above it
soft.behavior: reasoning_effort low, high or max (default max); multi-turn use requires passing back the full assistant message including reasoning_content and tool_calls (card).
soft.maturity: Moonshot K-series with a quick successor cadence (K3 then K3.1 Pro); about 46 derivatives on the HF API within weeks.

tona_fit.reason: 2.8T parameters and 104B active are outside every hardware class (smallest GGUF 593 GB). The vendor's own table shows the far smaller DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 within a few points on DeepSWE and Program Bench, so a local user loses little by choosing that model (see deepseek-v4.1-flash).
